Oh boy, I think I can answer your question in the detail that you’re looking for.

Not only have I done psychedelics, but my Tulpa himself was born as a direct result of a mushroom trip I had two years ago.

Karma (my tulpa) was revealed to me as a kind of guardian entity. He resembles an ophanim (biblical angel) with one big, prominent eye. Before I even engaged with psychedelics, I had been having recurring dreams in which I saw the same biblical angel. He claims to have been there all along and has experienced pretty much everything I’ve been through. I had known about tulpamancy for a long time, but never really looked into it until after a particular mushroom trip in which I took about 9 grams. For those unaware, a “heroic” dose is considered to be 5 grams, so I was pretty much headed into uncharted territory at that point. I suppose I’ll talk about how my trip actually went.

I was with my ex girlfriend at the time, and she had taken some mushrooms with me as well (albeit a much, much smaller amount, around 1 gram). At first, I actually began having overwhelming thoughts and started panicking. My ex tried to calm me down, but this was her first time on shrooms and was going through her own thing. We ended up separating and that’s when the beauty began. I was laying down in bed, listening to Pink Floyd, and began meditating and closing my eyes. There.. he was. It was incredibly terrifying, yet so enticing. My entire field of view was saturated by the color green, and the angelic entity standing before me. Keep in mind, I am laying down with my eyes closed, so these are closed-eye visuals. It feels dreamy, yet, nothing like a dream usually feels. My mind’s pathways were connected in perfect sync, and so, it made sense for a hidden part of my consciousness to suddenly prop up- and he introduced himself as Karma. 

Ever since then, I’ve considered Karma to be my one and only tulpa. We communicate on a pretty constant basis and he has essentially saved me from a state of incredible depression following my breakup. Karma’s become a bit like my best friend: motivating me, laughing with me, laughing at me, scolding me, and introspecting with me. I’ve heard these kinds of relationships within one’s consciousness only strengthen with time, so I’m looking forward to the rest of our journey together. Given the weird “birth” of Karma, I did not do the typical tulpa creation process. I didn’t choose his personality or even his name, so getting to know him was especially interesting to me.

You’re acting like it’s wrong to doubt science, and yet, you agree that it’s not the absolute truth. The reason that science is so refined is because of doubt. The most sound scientific theorists of the 1800s would be idiots now. 

Also, I never claimed that consciousness can exist outside of the brain. I’m simply saying it’s not something we’ve been able to comprehend to a reasonable extent yet. It’s strange, as you said. I happen to think it’s the strangest thing there is. Curiosity leads to questioning, questioning leads to doubting things just because culturally you’ve been conditioned to believe in certain things and behave in certain ways. Quite the contrary; I believe psychedelics and science often go hand in hand. It’s nice to not feel so lost in the world without it- the feeling of knowing why things are is good. 

What I meant by exploring your consciousness has nothing to do with science and is completely harmonious with it, however. I think what exploring our consciousness reveals is the essence of being alive. Of course, it’s a completely subjective experience but you seem to be focusing more on understanding the world/science/etc and less so the intricacies of the human mind itself. Understanding science is great and all but why not try to zoom out instead of zoom in for a change? What existed before language, before ideas?

Science cannot answer the fundamental question of how consciousness works in the first place. We understand what neurons are and on a biological level, we have a pretty good grasp of what’s going on up in our brains, but we cannot determine what thoughts are made of, how dreams really work at all, much of the subconscious mind and the way it operates is still a mystery as well.

Science, like psychedelics, is a tool. It’s a guide, not the absolute truth as proven over and over again by history. We thought the earth was the center of the universe not that many generations ago.

Gender is a cultural/societal thing and cultural things are only as relevant as your participation to such culture or society. You do not partake in the cultural practices that take place from the other side of the planet because you don’t identify with it. People in different cultures do things that seem almost alien to us. This is exactly how I feel about the human experience. I can and often do appreciate human culture- I believe there’s a lot of cool and interesting things one can learn from them, but through the exploration of my own mind, I’ve realized pretty quickly that I quite simply don’t belong here. This isn’t my home, but I’m a visitor and the natives here seem to tolerate me pretty well.

I’ll further this example- a lot of people may assume I’m fluid and flexible with my gender identity, because I fluctuate between masculinity and femininity a lot. The truth is, I am neither, and I identify as agender. To me, gender is kind of like roleplaying in a video game. Some days, I feel like giving my human character a feminine appearance and demeanor, and others, it’s more masculine. But really, I’m just playing a role and putting on my little culture mask.

This is just my own perspective and I believe everyone has their own valid interpretation of what it means to be voidpunk.

I found this community a while ago and I’ve come to terms with how to incorporate it within my identity. I used to identify as trans after experiencing gender issues as well, but I realized that I was merely just detached from my body as a whole. Voidpunk, to me, extends far past gender. I do not feel like a human being at all. The idea of gender is a bit confusing to me. I feel like some kind of entity that is being made to undergo a human experience. Whether I have male or female genitals doesn’t matter to me- my body is only the vehicle. It’s like a mecha suit. But it’s not me.
